title: Isocratic HPLC-PDA Separation of Ibuprofen and Selected Related Compounds Using Alcohol-Based Mobile Phases: Chromatographic Performance and Environmental Impact Assessment
content: In this study, three HPLC methods based on different organic solvents; namely, acetonitrile, methanol, and ethanol—each combined with aqueous acidic mobile phases, were developed and evaluated. Based on these investigations, a significantly greener, faster, and simpler isocratic HPLC-UV/PDA method was established. The compendial methods used for separation of ibuprofen from its related compounds typically use a C18 column operated at a flow rate of 2.0 mL min⁻¹, with analysis time of approximately 70 min. On contrast, the proposed method enables efficient separation of the pharmacopoeial ibuprofen-related compounds within a total analysis time of approximately 10 min or less. In our experiments, methanol not only reduced the environmental impact of the method but also provided chromatographic performance equal to or better than that obtained using acetonitrile. Excellent separations were achieved on both C18 and C8 stationary phases from different manufacturers, regardless of column dimensions or particle technology. Mobile phases containing approximately 68–75% methanol consistently provided adequate retention and baseline separation of the critical impurities, particularly Impurity A, ibuprofen, and Impurity B. Replacement of methanol with ethanol, an even greener solvent, is also feasible. However, the use of ethanol involves well-known chromatographic compromises resulting from its higher viscosity and lower elution strength. Therefore, improving the environmental sustainability of an HPLC method inevitably requires balancing chromatographic performance against environmental benefits.
